title: Gideon and the Sigil
premise: Emrys Delacroix, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Gideon, has spent their whole life in the valley where magic cannot follow — until the border wards collapse the night the stars go out, and the valley is dragged into a world that remembers what Gideon truly was: not a god, but the first sigil-bearer who sealed magic away to end an ancient war. Hunted by the resurrected Order of the Unbound, who want the seal broken, Emrys discovers the secret they carry is written into their own blood — they are Gideon's final ward, the last living piece of the seal. To save the valley, Emrys must choose between restoring the silent god and unmaking themselves, and in the end they do neither: they rewrite the sigil with their own name, becoming a new kind of guardian — mortal, flawed, and finally belonging to both worlds.
about_author: Elodie Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval grimoires before turning to fiction. They write from a drafty farmhouse, where the local folklore has a habit of creeping into everything they write.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot Magic
chapters.summary: Emrys takes a routine escort job along the border wards, establishing their life as a mercenary in a valley untouched by magic for three centuries. Through their weary, pragmatic POV, we see the quiet rituals of a people sworn to a god who never answers. Emotional beat: restless contentment on the edge of catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: The border wards fail at moonrise and the stars vanish one by one; Emrys, on watch, feels the valley's silence break for the first time in their life. POV shifts between Emrys and their captain, Halvard, as panic spreads. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a lifelong certainty shattering.

chapters.title: What Came Through the Wards
chapters.summary: Emrys and Halvard investigate the fallen ward-stones and find them not broken but unlocked — and a stranger dying among them, clutching a sigil that matches Emrys's birthmark. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the first hint that Emrys was always meant to be here.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Secret
chapters.summary: The stranger, a scholar of the Order of the Unbound, tells Emrys that Gideon was no god but the first sigil-bearer, and that the valley itself is the seal — with Emrys as its living keystone. He dies before explaining how to hold it. Emotional beat: the burden of a truth no one asked to carry.

chapters.title: Sworn to Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys hides the truth from the valley council, who vote to send riders to the capital for help. Emrys's POV reveals their fear that revealing their bloodline will make them a target — or a sacrifice. Emotional beat: isolation deepening even among their own people.

chapters.title: The Order of the Unbound
chapters.summary: The first Unbound agents enter the valley disguised as refugees, led by the charismatic Vess Corvane. Emrys recognizes the sigil-work on their gear and shadows them alone, learning the Order means to break the seal and free magic — whatever it costs. Emotional beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Halvard's Doubt
chapters.summary: Halvard catches Emrys lying about the night of the wards' fall. Their confrontation fractures a years-long bond, as Halvard demands loyalty to the valley and Emrys can't give the whole truth. Emotional beat: grief for a friendship that honesty might yet save.

chapters.title: Beyond the Border
chapters.summary: Emrys crosses the old ward-line for the first time, into a world where magic is real and the stars are dark, seeking answers at a ruined temple of Gideon. Emotional beat: awe and terror — the world is larger and crueler than the valley ever taught.

chapters.title: The Temple of the Silent God
chapters.summary: In the temple, Emrys experiences Gideon's silence firsthand — a presence that is not dead but withholding — and finds murals depicting a figure with their own birthmark. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your identity was authored by someone else.

chapters.title: Vess Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane intercepts Emrys and offers not violence but a bargain: join the Unbound, break the seal willingly, and keep your life and name. Emrys is tempted — the valley never truly wanted them. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging in the wrong place.

chapters.title: The Valley Bleeds
chapters.summary: Emrys returns to find the Unbound have struck the valley, draining the ward-stones and leaving the borderlands dying. Halvard is gravely wounded holding the line. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh — the secret Emrys kept has a body count.

chapters.title: Confession at the Ward-Stone
chapters.summary: Emrys confesses everything to the council and to a recovering Halvard: the bloodline, the stranger, the truth about Gideon. The valley's reaction is not the forgiveness or the fury Emrys expected, but fear. Emotional beat: the terrible cost of truth told too late.

chapters.title: The Keystones
chapters.summary: The council's archivist reveals old texts: the seal has three keystones, and one by one the Unbound are destroying them. Emrys realizes the final keystone is a person — themselves. Emotional beat: from bearer of a secret to bearer of a countdown.

chapters.title: Ride to the Second Stone
chapters.summary: Emrys, Halvard, and a small company race across the blighted borderlands to defend the second keystone, skirmishing with Unbound hunters. Emotional beat: camaraderie rebuilt in motion — Halvard chooses to trust Emrys again, without guarantees.

chapters.title: The Second Stone Falls
chapters.summary: They arrive too late; the second keystone is shattered, and the magic bleeding into the valley begins warping land and memory alike. A companion is lost to a corruption of the wild sigils. Emotional beat: failure that cannot be undone, and resolve hardened by it.

chapters.title: What Gideon Withholds
chapters.summary: The silent god finally speaks — a single, devastating message: breaking the seal was Gideon's own original sin, and Emrys was made to finish what Gideon could not. Emotional beat: betrayal by the divine; the mentor-figure revealed as the first liar.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: Emrys learns the seal can be rewritten — not restored, not broken — but only by someone willing to inscribe their own name into it and surrender their old identity entirely. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — identity as something chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: March of the Unbound
chapters.summary: Corvane's full force marches on the final ward-stone at the valley's heart, and the valley's people — farmers, smiths, soldiers — arm themselves for a battle they cannot win by strength. Emotional beat: a community choosing to stand for the outcast who once stood apart from them.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Last Ward
chapters.summary: The valley makes its stand; Halvard falls holding the line, buying Emrys the hour they need. Emrys cuts through the battle to confront Corvane at the stone. Emotional beat: sacrifice and fury intertwined; the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Emrys and Corvane duel amid the failing sigils; Corvane argues that magic's return is freedom, and Emrys — who never belonged anywhere — understands the longing. Emrys defeats her but refuses to kill her. Emotional beat: mercy as the final rejection of the war's old logic.

chapters.title: The New Sigil
chapters.summary: At the broken ward-stone, Emrys inscribes their own name over Gideon's, becoming the seal's living heart — mortal, present, answerable. Magic returns to the world, bounded and witnessed, and the stars come back. Emotional beat: transcendence through self-authorship; grief and birth in the same breath.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Months later, the valley lives between two worlds, and Emrys — changed, half-heard by the sigil they carry — walks its border as warden and neighbor both. Halvard's grave overlooks the wards; the silence is no longer empty. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging — an ending that is also a watch begun.
